correctness.rationale: PASS: The graph S(K_n) is exactly the singleton/doubleton incidence graph, whose metric on its two Boolean layers is Hamming |U triangle V| with five pair classes. Averaging Gram forms over S_n reduces the unrestricted Hilbert problem to two standard modes, the doubleton extra irreducible, and a centroid offset, with A,B,D,T>=0 and C²<=AB. For n>=5 a completed-square inequality gives delta_I >= (n-2)/(4(n-1)) delta_DD; since disjoint doubletons have distance 4, c2²>=4(n-2)/(n-1). For n=4, optimizing B>=4 and the nonincident distance>=9 gives the sharp quadratic root (43-8sqrt19)/3; for n=3 standard mode gives 9/4. The centered coordinate realization matches each bound. An independent construction and pairwise distortion test verified 6,003 unordered pairs through n=11; it does not replace the all-n Gram lower bounds.

evidence: The 2021 exact Euclidean graph distortion results are for distance-regular families; S(K_n) has two vertex degrees when n>=4. The 2008 work classifies partial-cube subdivisions, not known from available text to optimize Hilbert distortion.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Do not import a sharp distortion of the entire Hamming cube or Johnson layer to a selected bipartite union of layers; submetric least distortion may be smaller. The specialized invariant Gram bound is not supplied by cited stronger results.

The older exact same-graph Hamming paper's complete text was inaccessible, leaving a material risk of an unmentioned Euclidean consequence; the available abstract only proves partial-cube classification.
